text: The US bid that led $BTC has flipped. From July to the September breakout, US trading hours drove most of Bitcoin's gains. Since then, the US session has been a net seller. The full picture, from ETF flows to liquidations, in this week's Week On-chain 👇
Bitcoin got through the $85K wall, but the rally is running light. Our new Week On-chain maps what is missing, what altcoins are doing and the levels to watch.

Large entities are back in profit. Small wallets stayed in profit the whole time: at the June low, $BTC held well above their $48K cost basis while sharks and whales slipped underwater. In the 2022 bear market, price fell below every group's cost basis.

$BTC trades near $86k after a Sunday rally lifted the weekly close about 2% higher. Derivatives positioning eased back into its normal range and ETF inflows cooled, while on-chain activity, new capital and profit-taking all run hot. https://glassno.de/4zctuPd

Whales have stopped sending $BTC to exchanges. Their summer run of net deposits lasted over three months, twice as long as any other since 2023. It ended in late August, and the flow has stayed negative since.
